authoredNote: line_number values transcribed from the numbered source and then checked against a run: VPATH on 16, CFLAGS on 17, .DEFAULT_GOAL on 19, target `all` on 20. The `CFLAGS -> VPATH` reference and the two prerequisite edges are all on their own lines (17 and 20).
rationale: MAKE-G1. `VPATH = src:include` is the ASSIGNMENT spelling of the search path, and the sibling `vpath %.c src` DIRECTIVE had been recorded all along — so the two spellings of one feature were deliberately asymmetric, pending corpus evidence that never came (0 occurrences in 100 pinned files). The asymmetry was not cosmetic. Because `VPATH` was never declared, a reference to it fell to `uses`, the class this lane reserves for names that NOTHING can declare — yet in a file that sets `VPATH`, this file is precisely the thing that declares it. CFLAGS on line 17 reads the search path and was published as a read of something undeclared. `VPATH` is a GNU Make builtin whose value a makefile may set, exactly like CURDIR or MAKEFILE_LIST, so it is now a `constant` and the reference is a `references` edge. The directories are kept as a LIST because the value is colon-separated on the page and a consumer asking where the makefile looks for a prerequisite wants the list, not the spelling.

forbidRelationships.note: THE DEFECT. `uses` is the class for a name nothing can declare; this file declares VPATH on line 16, so the read on line 17 is a `references` edge. Pre-fix the assignment was not modelled at all and this edge was published as `uses`, which is the lane's own definition of asserting a declaration that does not exist — stated backwards.
VPATH is a make variable, not a buildable TARGET. `exports` is the module's edge for what the file provides to be built or included, and a search path is neither.

a search path does not reference its own directories. `VPATH = src` means "look in src", and publishing `VPATH -> src` would read as a dependency, which is the category error the dangle adjudication exists to prevent.
